snapshot.scope_description: Declared design for a personal notes CRUD app: a browser client, one service, one database, session authentication, and per-user note authorization.
omissions: This is an architecture example, not an implemented or deployed notes application.
Registration, password recovery, deployment, and operational hardening are outside this example.

entities.label: Notes frontend
entities.description: A browser UI for sign-in and creating, listing, editing, and deleting personal notes.

entities.label: Notes service
entities.description: The only backend service. Handles sessions and notes CRUD, validates the session, and filters every note operation by its owner.

entities.label: App database
entities.description: One database containing notes (with owner IDs), users, and server-side sessions.

entities.label: Session API
entities.description: Sign-in and sign-out endpoints. Verifies credentials and issues or revokes an opaque server-side session; no note operations live here.

entities.label: Notes API
entities.description: Create, list, read, update, and delete notes. Every operation requires a valid session and enforces per-user ownership.

entities.label: Authentication
entities.description: The frontend presents sign-in. The service validates opaque server-side sessions on notes requests.

entities.label: Owner-only notes
entities.description: Server-side ownership checks restrict listing and individual read/update/delete operations to the current user; created notes receive that user as owner.

relations.label: Sign in / out
relations.description: The browser requests session creation or termination.
relations.condition: When the user signs in or signs out.

relations.label: Notes CRUD
relations.description: Create, list, read, update, or delete a note using the current session.

relations.label: Read
relations.description: Read notes scoped to the current user; read users and sessions as required by authentication.

relations.label: Write
relations.description: Insert, update, and delete notes; create and revoke sessions. Note changes enforce ownership.
The notes service implements credential checks and session validation.
The same notes service enforces ownership for every note operation.
